source_name: AJPES – Ponovna uporaba podatkov PRS / web services for developers
why_relevant: Documents the machine channels (wsPRS and related web services) for reusing business-register data in a client's own system — the legitimate, contractual route to bulk company data instead of scraping ePRS.

source_name: AJPES FI-PO / proFI-PO – financial data and indicators from annual reports (re-use channel)
why_relevant: Structured, field-level financial data extracted from filed annual reports (plus unpaid-liability flags), available as a web service or bulk delivery. Turns the PDF annual-report corpus into machine-readable financials for banks and payments vendors — the highest-leverage A1 asset if budget allows.

source_name: AJPES eObjave – official electronic announcements (court/business register entries, insolvency, company notices)
why_relevant: Publishes registration decisions, founding/amendment documents, statutory company announcements and insolvency proceedings. Reveals ownership changes, capital increases, mergers, new payment-services subsidiaries and distress events for banks' suppliers — corporate-event intelligence that never appears in an annual report.

source_name: Sodni register / court register document collection via AJPES
why_relevant: Since Feb 2008 the underlying documents behind register entries (articles of association, court decisions, filed deeds) are published. Gives primary evidence of corporate structure and shareholder changes for Slovenian banks and fintech/payment entities.

source_name: OPSI – Poslovni register Slovenije open dataset (podatki.gov.si)
why_relevant: Free, licence-clean bulk extract of PRS basic data (registration number, full name, address, legal form, registering body), refreshed roughly twice monthly in XML/CSV. The cheapest legitimate way to build and refresh the Slovenian entity master list that everything else joins to.

source_name: SEOnet – Ljubljana Stock Exchange regulated-information feed (Slovene)
why_relevant: The mandated publication venue for regulated information of LJSE-listed issuers — NLB, other financial issuers and listed suppliers post annual/interim reports, earnings, inside information and financial-calendar items here first. Highest-timeliness A1 artefact stream in Slovenia.

source_name: SEOnet English interface (Ljubljana Stock Exchange announcements, EN)
why_relevant: Many issuers post an English version of the same regulated announcement; useful for downstream NLP and for cross-checking Slovene originals without translation loss on numbers.

source_name: Ljubljana Stock Exchange – List of Issuers
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of every issuer on the exchange market with links to their regulated information — the seed list for which Slovenian financial-sector companies have continuous disclosure obligations at all.

source_name: Ljubljanska borza – Finančni koledar (issuer financial calendar)
why_relevant: Forward calendar of issuer results dates, general meetings and dividend events. Lets collection be scheduled ahead of earnings releases rather than discovered after the fact. Exact deep-link URL not confirmed in this pass — enter from the LJSE homepage/sitemap.

source_name: LJSE INFO HRAMBA – officially appointed mechanism (OAM) for storing regulated information
why_relevant: The storage mechanism behind SEOnet: defines how regulated information is captured and archived and how third parties access it. Reading the rules tells a collector what the guaranteed retention, format and metadata are — and whether the OAM, not SEOnet, is the better long-term archive endpoint.

source_name: ATVP – Registri (Securities Market Agency registers: prospectuses, issuer reports)
why_relevant: The securities regulator maintains registers of approved prospectuses and of issuers' audited annual and semi-annual reports / regulated-information filings. Prospectuses are dense primary sources on bank funding, ownership and business model that never appear in AJPES.

source_name: OAM.si – publicly accessible register of issuers' audited annual and semi-annual reports
why_relevant: ATVP documentation states the register of issuers' audited annual reports, semi-annual reports and regulated-information reports is publicly accessible free of charge at www.oam.si. If it functions as described it is a second, regulator-side archive of exactly the A1 artefacts, complementary to SEOnet.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Seznam notifikacij plačilnih institucij (PSD2 passporting notifications, PDF catalogue)
why_relevant: Lists foreign payment institutions notified to operate in Slovenia — the inbound-competition view that no domestic filing register captures. Directly relevant to sizing the payments market and spotting new entrants.

source_name: e-Justice portal – Slovenia business registers page (BRIS entry point)
why_relevant: EU-level description of and gateway to the Slovenian register, including the BRIS interconnection. Useful for cross-border lookups of Slovenian entities and for confirming which register is legally authoritative for which document type.

source_name: Issuer-side SEOnet mirrors (e.g. NLB investor announcements page)
why_relevant: Listed issuers republish their SEOnet filings on their own IR pages, often with cleaner HTML, English versions and longer archives than the exchange feed. A useful redundancy layer if SEOnet crawling is rate-limited or restructured.

source_name: SeeNews — Slovenia country feed
why_relevant: SEE-focused business wire that systematically summarises Slovenian bank results, M&A, ratings actions and regulator statements in English for an investor audience; frequently the English rendering of Slovenian-only releases (e.g. NLB/Addiko bid steps, OTP Slovenia results, Gorenjska Banka stake purchases).

source_name: bne IntelliNews — Slovenia coverage
why_relevant: Emerging-Europe investor wire with dense, dated Slovenian bank coverage (NLB takeover bids, NPL portfolio sales, ECB bond redemption approvals, deposit pricing). Good for narrative continuity and for catching regulatory approvals reported only in Slovenian elsewhere.

source_name: STA English Service (Slovenian Press Agency)
why_relevant: The national news agency's in-house English service (since 1994) is the canonical translation layer for Slovenian business, banking and economic-policy news; most English-language coverage of Slovenia downstream (Slovenia Times, international pickup) originates here. Explicit editorial focus on operations of Slovenian firms and economic policy.

source_name: The Slovenia Times
why_relevant: STA-powered English news portal on Slovenia; the most accessible free English restatement of domestic banking, privatisation and payments stories, useful for cross-checking Slovenian-only sources without a wire subscription.

source_name: Total Slovenia News — banking tag
why_relevant: Independent English-language Slovenia news aggregator/translator with a dedicated banking tag; lower authority than STA but often carries translated summaries of Slovenian press (Delo, Finance, Dnevnik) that are otherwise paywalled or SL-only.

source_name: Bloomberg — Slovenia banking articles
why_relevant: Covers Slovenian bank strategy and sector-level rating moves for a global investor audience (e.g. NLB Balkan M&A ambitions, Fitch outlook revisions on Slovenian banks); frequently the first English-language framing of management commentary given in Slovenian.

source_name: Reuters — Slovenia / NLB tagged coverage
why_relevant: Global wire baseline for Slovenian sovereign/bank events (privatisation, EU state-aid decisions, takeover bids). Reuters items propagate into every downstream aggregator, so they are the de-facto reference version of an event in English.

source_name: S&P Global Market Intelligence — CEE banking news
why_relevant: Analyst-grade English coverage of Slovenian bank strategy and deals (e.g. NLB's Croatia entry via Addiko), with balance-sheet context that pure news wires lack; also the publisher of S&P rating actions on NLB.

source_name: Fitch Ratings — Slovenian bank rating actions
why_relevant: Primary English-language issuer of rating action commentaries on Slovenian banks and the sovereign; these RACs are original English documents that pre-date and drive the regional press items, making them a clean upstream anchor for the translation/aggregation layer.

source_name: NLB Group — international/English media centre and investor relations
why_relevant: The issuer's own English site is the authoritative translated release layer: press releases, investor news, financial calendar and IR events published in parallel with the Slovenian originals. Directly on-topic for disclosures, annual reports, IR and earnings.

source_name: Ljubljana Stock Exchange SEOnet (English interface)
why_relevant: Official regulated-disclosure portal for LJSE issuers with an English interface; carries NLB and other financial-sector announcements under MAR Art.17 / ZTFI. Note the explicit caveat that only the Slovene text has legal value — so it is both a translation layer and a flag that SL originals must be read.

source_name: Investegate — NLB (LSE/RNS) company announcements
why_relevant: NLB's GDRs trade in London, so its regulatory announcements are also filed in English via RNS and archived free on Investegate — an unpaywalled English mirror of Slovenian issuer disclosures (bond issuance, takeover offers).

source_name: Banka Slovenije — English site (publications & media posts)
why_relevant: The central bank publishes full English translations of the Financial Stability Review/Report, banking-system monthly data and press posts. This is the highest-authority translated primary material in the cell and the benchmark against which press summaries can be checked.
